evidence_families.population: Creator videos eligible for official Studio Collaborations feature
evidence_families.method: Current first-party Help instructions, not platform-wide feature adoption statistics

evidence_families.population: Historical release announcement for initial rollout
evidence_families.method: Product announcement, not an experiment or creator population sample

evidence_families.population: U.S. online survey respondents ages 14–29 (N=496) and ages 14–44 (N=939), different question sets
evidence_families.method: YouTube-commissioned NRG survey with question-level respondent counts, recruitment probabilities and uncertainty not publicly verified

evidence_families.population: Editorially highlighted videos and cultural topics, not randomly selected posts
evidence_families.method: YouTube Culture & Trends year-end editorial examples

evidence_families.population: 393 title-filtered pre-recorded YouTube study-with-me videos and 164,611 associated selected comments
evidence_families.method: 2024 public API title-query selection, post-collection filtering, topic modeling and sentiment classification; selected public comment events are not unique people

collaboration_policy.discovery_intent: May recommend collaboration upload to both the uploading channel and collaborators' audiences

questions.meaning: Perception that YouTube creators are widely known
Perception that memes are widely known
Self-report having watched videos unpacking stories in fandom
Self-report watching content from a self-described niche community
Agreement that a fan subject's success feels like respondent's own success
Agreement with pride in helping the fan subject achieve success
Agreement that YouTube is the best place to explore personal interests
Agreement that YouTube keeps interest long after discovery

survey_shared_limits.source_family: One YouTube/NRG 2026 commissioned research family, with separate age-specific question groups; not eight independent datasets

illustrative_cross_channel_forms.format: Fan remakes, skits, reinterpretations and theory videos linked to television franchises
Fancams and fan-created narratives reframing fictional artists and songs
Independent creators' Roblox game trends adapted as video-community topics

study_protocol.unit: Publicly observed content item plus explicit accepted collaborator relationship, not a deduced private viewer migration
study_protocol.design: Pre-register fixed genre/country/date strata, sample eligible channels and independent creators, record uploads with and without collaborators, and separately report selected/nonselected and missing data.
study_protocol.comparison: Require truly comparable 30- and 90-day pre/post windows with publication cadence, content topic, channel size, viewing metric revisions and observed promotion accounted for; do not equate association with causal lift.
conditions: Use officially public/authorized source records, no individual viewer profiling
Do not collect unpublished collaboration invitations, revenue contracts or private analytics
Public followers and collaborators can overlap; subscriptions are not deduplicated people
Do not infer who first invented a meme from timestamps of a selectively found sample
A mention, remix or recurring trope does not prove causal audience migration
Audio/video copyright, attribution and license restrictions still apply

acceptance_gates.limitations: Current official Help and prior announcement establish differing numerical product ceilings
Single commissioned research family; no probability-based population generalization
No selected or random creator video sample and disclosure of collaboration adoption
No verified unique-person overlaps or access-authorized analytics
No measured collaboration costs, payouts or comparable untreated creators

study_with_me_observation.selection: Prerecorded YouTube videos matched title phrase 'study with me' in September 2024 through the public YouTube Data API
source_limitations: Title search selected videos explicitly named 'study with me' and excludes other formats, names and silent/noncommenting viewers.
The published article's analyzed comment count is a comment-event count, not a count of unique commenters or verified learners.
Sentiment and study-habit claims are machine-coded text, not personally verified mental states, education gains or clinical outcomes.
Publication-date and comment-sample availability may bias videos toward visible, searchable material; the sample is not a worldwide YouTube content or audience census.
No retrieved raw comments, usernames, channel identities, transcripts or minors' records are republished.
Selection is observational, so causal video-design or creator-earnings effects are not established.
